items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I liked them when Fred Astaire sang them

ctx.x: But you’re not talking about chord changes, you’re talking about like emotional—

No I’m talking about structure changes, emotional. The vividness and the drama again is really what I think I was caught up with originally. And the sort of maturity and the subtlety of a Lockjaw Davis or a Jimmy Forrest was a little bit lost on me. Because I didn’t have any connection to the source material that they were taking off from. I mean I heard that is, American standards are corny; not necessarily corny. I liked them when Fred Astaire sang them, but I didn’t feel like this is a vehicle for spilling out…
You’ve mentioned the vocal connection. People, instrumentalists, using vocal — loss for words here — vocal inflections.
